name: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Cloud Run
request: Create a small, playable Sky Steps checkpoint parkour game for one player on desktop and touch. Build one coherent short course with three ordered checkpoints, a moving-platform crossing, a clearly marked fall hazard, and a finish. Players must physically traverse it; touching a later checkpoint early must not skip progress. Reaching a checkpoint shows visible activation animation and synchronized confirmation sound. Falling returns the player to the last valid checkpoint without losing progress. Show the current checkpoint and elapsed run time, then a completion result and deliberate replay control. Search Marketplace first for reusable checkpoint, moving-platform and course components, preserving useful existing behavior, visuals, motion and media. Inspect what is included and integrate missing rules rather than replacing working components wholesale. Use Marketplace audio and verify it actually plays. If a suitable component cannot be imported faithfully, record that capability gap. Use compact readable geometry and comfortable jumps; choose reasonable style and layout yourself. No multiplayer, saving, purchases or sprawling map. Success needs native traversal, ordered progression, moving-platform behavior, fall recovery, finish/replay and legible desktop/touch UI. A decorative obstacle scene or a timer alone is insufficient.

assetNeeds.constraints: Inspect every script and dependency; reject unsafe numeric requires or HTTP loaders. Must support physical character contact, visible activation, and auditable media. Each checkpoint should fit compact platforms within roughly 12 studs. Do not assume its progression rules are correct until tested.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the primary progression landmarks and immediate reward feedback that teach and pace the Sky Steps run.

Activation animation, lights, particles, or color response

assetNeeds.constraints: Inspect motion implementation, network ownership assumptions, collision, rider behavior, cycle cleanup, scripts, and dependencies. It must remain rideable during native play and fit a crossing no larger than about 24 studs. Preserve verified motion rather than recreating it.

intent.experienceRole: Creates the course's central timing challenge and a visually obvious change from static jumping.
intent.interaction: The player waits for, boards, rides, and exits the moving platform to reach the next section; motion continues predictably after falls and respawns.
reusableFeatures: Rideable collision and character carrying behavior

assetNeeds.role: Reusable compact sky or cloud obby course component supplying coordinated platforms, landmarks, finish presentation, and hazard-readable visuals without expanding scope.
assetNeeds.constraints: Inspect for a coherent small-scale platform set, safe collisions, comfortable jump spacing, checkpoint or finish pieces, hazard markings, scripts, dependencies, and embedded media. Retain useful coordinated geometry only within the supplied namespace; do not import unrelated stages, monetization, saving, leaderboards, or sprawling map systems.

intent.experienceRole: Establishes a cohesive sky-parkour identity and readable physical route instead of disconnected primitive obstacles.
intent.interaction: The player runs and jumps across its safe surfaces toward visible checkpoint and finish landmarks. Geometry must support traversal; decorative elements must not obstruct or falsely imply a safe route.
reusableFeatures: Existing course scripts and media for audit

assetNeeds.role: Marketplace confirmation sound for accepted checkpoints if no faithfully imported checkpoint component includes suitable verified audio.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must have Marketplace provenance and pass loading, playback, and listening checks in the experience. Prefer a short, clear, nonverbal success cue suitable for synchronized checkpoint activation. Do not use generated, procedural, built-in, placeholder, inaccessible, or invented audio. This need remains blocked if verification cannot complete.

intent.experienceRole: Confirms that the player's physical checkpoint touch was valid and distinguishes accepted progress from an out-of-order touch.
intent.interaction: The sound begins when the server accepts a checkpoint and the visible checkpoint activation starts; it remains silent for rejected touches, falls, and ordinary platform contact.

spec.assetStrategy:
Discover complete reusable checkpoint, moving-platform, and sky-course Models before designing replacements. Audit their exact hierarchies, scripts, dependencies, triggers, motion, animation, collision, lifecycle behavior, and embedded media. Preserve verified checkpoint presentation, platform motion, coordinated course geometry, and audio where they satisfy the requested loop. Imported progression or recovery logic is retained only where source review and native tests establish compatibility with strict three-step ordering, authoritative timing, fall recovery, finish gating, and replay.

The exact integration scripts for checkpoint triggers, moving-platform interfaces, world presentation, and server state remain discovery-dependent and therefore are not preassigned. After inspection, add only narrow glue needed to enforce missing rules, with exclusive script ownership inside the supplied namespace. If the selected checkpoint component has no suitable verified sound, separately retrieve the checkpoint confirmation Audio need and verify loading, playback, permissions, audibility, and synchronization. Unsupported serialization, inaccessible source, unsafe dependencies, incompatible animation, lost embedded behavior, or audio that cannot be heard is a recorded capability gap and blocked requirement, not authorization for a procedural replacement.
spec.title: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Cloud Run
spec.summary:
Create a compact single-player sky parkour course inside the supplied namespace. The route begins on a safe floating launch island around Y=100, advances through three checkpoints in strict order, crosses a moving platform over a visibly dangerous fall zone, and ends at a distinct finish platform. Comfortable jumps use broad landing surfaces and short, readable gaps rather than precision-heavy obstacles.

First-minute journey: from spawn, the player sees the first checkpoint ahead, cyan route markers, the moving-platform crossing in the middle distance, and the gold finish beacon beyond it. The first jumps teach ordinary traversal. Touching checkpoint 1 produces an obvious activation pulse and synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The player then rides the moving platform, continues through checkpoints 2 and 3, and reaches the finish. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the latest valid checkpoint while preserving progress and the active timer. Completion freezes the result and requires the player to deliberately choose Replay before a new run begins.

The server owns ordered progression, checkpoint positions, run timing, completion, replay validation, touch debounces, fall detection, and recovery. The client owns the readable HUD and replay input but cannot award progress or choose teleport destinations. Replicated server state provides an initial snapshot and observable changes so HUD state is not lost or missed during character respawns.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and course systems must be discovered and inspected before integration. Their useful audited geometry, behavior, motion, animation, and media are retained. Missing rules are added as narrowly scoped glue after imported interfaces are known. Marketplace audio must load, play, and be heard during native checkpoint traversal. Unsupported scripts, dependencies, animation formats, or audio references are recorded as capability gaps rather than silently replaced. No persistence, purchases, combat, multiplayer competition, or sprawling secondary areas are included.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a bright, readable sky-island style with compact floating platforms, pale stone or white cloud-like structural surfaces, cyan route accents, warm gold finish accents, and high-contrast red/orange hazard markings. Platforms should use clean beveled or layered silhouettes rather than thin featureless slabs. Keep the route visible in sections from major landmarks so players can anticipate where to go next.

Compose the course along one gently turning forward route approximately 120–150 studs long and 35–50 studs wide. Spawn sits on a safe 16–22 stud landing island. Ordinary gaps should generally be about 5–8 studs with landing widths around 8–14 studs. The moving-platform crossing should be visually isolated over the hazard and have generous boarding and exit ledges. Checkpoints are unmistakable pads, rings, gates, or beacons placed directly on the traversal route. The finish uses a gold beacon or arch visible from earlier sections.

The hazard is not an ambiguous empty gap: use red/orange edge bands, warning chevrons, glow, particles, or another inspected component treatment around the fall area while retaining open sightlines to the sky below. Safe route surfaces remain cyan and white and must not visually resemble the hazard.

Checkpoint feedback visibly changes an accepted checkpoint through inspected existing animation or compatible pulse, light, color, or scale behavior added only if the retained component lacks it. The visual response and confirmation sound begin together when the server accepts the checkpoint. Later checkpoints touched out of order provide no activation or progress feedback.

The HUD is compact and high contrast. Current progress such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3” and an elapsed MM:SS.hh timer remain near the top edge without blocking traversal. Completion uses a centered result card with final time and a large Replay button. The button is comfortably tappable on touch and selectable on desktop. Layouts respect safe-area insets and remain legible at common phone and desktop resolutions.
